Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

evidence noun

facts that show something is true

also proof, be evidence that, sign that

classical

Cic. Att. 10.12a.3: mihi argūmentō est rēctē esse in Hispāniīs
Cic. Phil. 2.40: magnō argūmentō est

argūmentum, argūmentī n.

noun, second declension

evidence, proof; a sign from which something is inferred

Lewis & Short: proof that rests on facts, where ratiō rests on reasoning. Argūmentō esse, to be evidence (that), with an accusative and infinitive. A sign or clue that points to something is indicium (see sign); evidence given in court is testimōnium (see evidence, in court).

Other words

  • documentum, documentī n. — a proof, a lesson, an example: documentō esse, to show

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Traupman 366: documentō est; Sall. Cat. 9.4 (Lewis & Short): quārum rērum maxuma documenta haec habeō

    Classically not a document but something that teaches: a lesson, an example, a proof (Lewis & Short).

  • indicium, indiciī n. — proof, evidence (above all of guilt), information laid

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Sall. C. 52.36: convictus indiciō alicujus (Lewis & Short); Traupman 366

Examples

  • Massiliēnsium factum cum ipsum per sē lūculentum est tum mihi argūmentō est rēctē esse in Hispāniīs.

    What the people of Massilia have done is splendid in itself, and it is also evidence to me that things are going well in Spain.Cic. Att. 10.12a.3

  • quod autem idem maestitiam meam reprehendit, idem jocum, magnō argūmentō est mē in utrōque fuisse moderātum

    and the fact that the same man finds fault both with my gloom and with my joking is strong evidence that I kept the mean in bothCic. Phil. 2.40

See also evidence, prove, sign, fact.
